figures.caption: Per-slice wall of the tracked read at the diverted 550-cell state on one H200, against the number of slices in the batch. The dotted line is the 0.2 ms bound; the series is the minimum of 20 steady-state calls at each batch size.

rubric.contrast: defect: the bound's grey text and dotted line are #929292 on white, a contrast ratio of about 3.1:1, below the 4.5:1 that 14 pt text needs; the one numeric label for the figure's central threshold is the faintest mark on the page
rubric.data_ink: pass: one blue 3 pt series with markers carries the picture, its end value is directly labelled, and the only ruled element is the bound line itself
rubric.decoration: pass: no gridlines, no background fill, no gradient and no shading; the top and right spines are absent and only the two scaled axes are drawn
rubric.label_collision: pass: the direct label '9.379 ms at 16' clears both the line and its marker at batch 16, the bottom-left bound label clears the '1' tick label and the y-axis, and no text is clipped at any edge, with the x-axis label and the y-axis label complete
rubric.legibility: defect: the four measured per-slice walls (54.6, 20.2, 9.38 and 5.82 ms at batches 1, 4, 16 and 64) read at a glance, but the 0.2 ms bound the figure and its caption turn on cannot be located: on a 0 to about 65 ms linear axis the dotted reference line falls inside the x-axis stroke, so a reader sees a second line hugging the baseline rather than a threshold 29x below the last point
rubric.table_form: pass: four ordered batch sizes plotted as a falling trend, which is a relationship and not a table image; the same four rows are carried as a table above the figure in the fragment

findings.summary: The 0.2 ms bound is drawn at y=0.2 on an axis whose top is max(per_slice)*1.2, about 65 ms, so the dotted reference line at line 51 renders inside the x-axis stroke and is indistinguishable from zero. The figure exists to show that no batch size reaches the bound, and the gap it is about - a factor of 29 at 64 slices, 47 at 16 - is the one quantity the picture cannot show; the caption's 'The dotted line is the 0.2 ms bound' points a reader at a line that looks like the axis itself. A log y-scale, or a stated break, would let the bound and the data share one panel; reported, not edited, under this review's read-only fence.

The bound label is drawn in GREY (#929292) at 14 pt on white, a contrast ratio of about 3.1:1 against the 4.5:1 that text at that size needs to pass AA. Against the blue series and the dark tick labels the grey recedes as intended for a reference mark, but it is applied to text, and that text is the only place the reader is given the bound's value; the dotted line beside it inherits the same weakness.
